placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the south face of blk_randolph_market, the block's Washington Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is the closest line the plat module's own margin allows and is not a measurement of this frontage, and its west wall is fixed by the west end of the run's own frontage, 1.5 m clear of the side lot line at that end. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at Washington Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.
placement.symbolic_location: Anonymous reconstructed roof in the South Division block bounded by Randolph, Franklin, Washington and Market; standing ON the Washington Street frontage itself, one unit of the party-line row along it

persons.name: Tobias Beger
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Beger, Tobias' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.

persons.name: George W. Snow
persons.note: THE TOWN'S FIRST SURVEYOR AND ASSESSOR, WHICH IS AS CLOSE AS THE 1833 TOWN COMES TO A CENSUS-TAKER. An assessor's roll for 1834 or 1835 would settle a great deal of what this programme has had to infer, and none is in data/sources/. Andreas vol. 1, printed p. 132 (scan p. 281), 'an imperfect list of the denizens of the town in the fall of 1833, not before named' - a name, a trade and usually an arrival year, compiled fifty years after the fact. A YEAR off it is documented; a MONTH is not, and neither is anything about 1835. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 2 times: Tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833 — “Snow, George W.” (tax_1833_096, line 148); Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Snow, George W.” (poll_1834_102, line 271). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Snow' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “George W. Snow,” (f1839_v0139, printed page 42, ward 1, voting for John H. Kinzie). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Snow' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins G. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 3 times, as “SNOW GEORGE W”, 1833-10-24 to 1836-06-29: 1 lot in the platted town — lot 1 of block 7 in the town the register codes CHI (L1BL7CHI, as printed) and 2 parcels of the school section — BL46 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL55 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read, 5.51 acres stated in all, for $1979.00 (ls0334, ls0335, ls1460). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE SCHOOL-SECTION ROWS ARE GROUND INSIDE THE TOWN, NOT FARMLAND: section 16 of T39N R14E was platted and sold off by lot and by block at the sale of 1833, which is why the register states 0000.00 acres against most of them. Ground inside the town is nearer to this reconstruction than a quarter-section is, and it is still a purchase: the register names a purchaser and never an occupant, and nothing here puts this person on that ground. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $1730.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: SNOW GEORGE W matches George W. Snow: the forename names George W. Snow of the 2 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

residents.research_note: THE MAN WHOSE PAPERWORK WOULD HAVE ANSWERED THIS PROGRAMME'S QUESTIONS. Snow is also the name attached in the Chicago literature to the balloon frame, which this dataset's structure records treat with care: data/structures/exchange_coffee_house.json notes that balloon framing 'was developed in Chicago in 1832-33, so an 1834 building could be either' and chooses braced framing as the conservative reading. Nothing in this household supports or refutes the attribution and it is recorded here as a lead, not a finding.

frontage.why: T-0317, the successor T-0028's programme owes, and the first parcel in this project where the core density standard's corner clause and the end rule point in OPPOSITE directions. THE FACE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, by the command T-A14 made of it — tools/measure_street_frontage.py randolph washington market franklin — and on the committed dataset Randolph carries 7 documented records and 7 inferred households against Washington's 1 and 0, Market's 2 and 1, and Franklin's 2 and 1. Randolph is this block's business face by the town's own record and it is FULL: the first deal took lots 0 and 2 and the inferred-household layer's two sawyer dwellings hold 4 and 6, so every lot on that face carries a roof and the two lots this block has left are both on the Washington tier. WHAT BINDS IS THE STANDARD'S THIRD CLAUSE. Lot 1 is the block's one free CORNER lot, the south-west one, fronting Washington along its long edge and Market Street along its short one, and a corner lot BUILDS TO THE CORNER — an east-anchored run packs back toward the middle of the face and stops wherever its roofs run out, so the corner is the one piece of frontage a row can never reach. The run is packed WEST to it. AND THE GRADING RUNS THE OTHER WAY, which is the finding here. On blk_randolph_dearborn's third deal the free corner was at Dearborn — the only crossing of the main stem in July 1835 — so building to the corner and standing the best roof nearest the crossing were the same act, and the parcel could not tell the two clauses apart. This corner is at MARKET, the far end of the face from that bridge, so they separate: the corner clause fixes WHERE THE ROW STANDS and the end rule fixes WHICH ROOF STANDS WHERE IN IT, and on this block they are demonstrably different questions. THE END RULE IS READ, NOT ASSERTED: tools/measure_end_rule.py reads this face at a spread of 71.03 m and a unit step of 6.07 m under the walked criterion and grades on it, while the same face under T-A11's straight line reads 4.82 m and is BELOW THE FLOOR — so the walk is what makes a grading possible here at all, and the straight line would have been grading this parcel's own declared setback invention. The row is therefore graded EAST, toward Franklin and the bridge beyond it: the meanest dwelling stands on the corner and the best closes the run at the east end. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing, the lot's own stretch of it and the end the run packs toward are all read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the 1.5 m setback is the plat module's own lot margin rather than a measurement of this frontage. The Washington face carries no committed street wall for the run to adopt — the two roofs already standing on that tier are one-per-lot placements set back inside their own lots — so this run is the first line on the face and states the margin rather than adopting one.
